MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 28, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley at 5:00 p.m., on February 28, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 24, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell (arrived via teleconference from Waikoloa, Hawaii 5:12 pm)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith
  Rattay; City Attorney William Curley; Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz;
  Labor Attorney Peter Brown: Employee Organization: Service Employees’
  International Union (SEIU)

City Council Minutes  1  February 28, 2023
 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Pending Litigation: People ex. rel. Schlesinger v.
  Sachs, et. al., OCSC No. 30-2022-01262431-CU-JR-CJC

  Council Member Bucknum announced that she will recuse herself from this item.

  Cathy Schlicht, M/V.: Stated the lack of a historical record that shows how the prior Council
  put the City in jeopardy with the lack of transparency. She criticized the City Attorney for
  creating a process for a desired outcome and referenced an email that she sent in 2020 to the
  Council.

CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel - Pending Litigation: Schlesinger v. Mission Viejo,
  OCSC Case No. 30-2022-01253878-CU-WM-CJC

  Cathy Schlicht, M/V.: Criticized the City Manger for his lack of involvement in the whole
  election process and to allow the legal shenanigans. She stated that the 2022 elections are
  over and in her opinion the City Attorney filed the appeal to protect himself from malpractice.

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he wanted to make the record clear that the speaker
misunderstands the law and the procedural history. He recapped the court meeting with Judge
Schwarm and plaintiff attorney Kevin Shenkman.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:09 pm, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley recessed to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:04 pm with four City Council Members present and Mayor Goodell joined via
teleconference.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley, announced that we had three closed session items that were taken in reverse
order. CS3 is a pending litigation on a writ case with an offer presented from the plaintiffs and we
will not be advancing that which was unanimous decision by the City Council. CS2 is a similar
offer that we will not be advancing. CS1 was not heard due to time and will be re-agendized at a
future council meeting.

INVOCATION: Council Member Ruesch

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tom Moore, M.V.: Supports a Specific Plan for not only the Core Area Vision Plan but also the
area from Interstate 5 on the West, Veterans Way on the Est, Jeronimo Road on the North and Oso
Parkway on the South.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley asked staff to perhaps have a review of the 2007 Urban Land Institute
study at a future meeting.
City Council Minutes  2  February 28, 2023
 Walt Lawson, M.V.: He stated that the City owes an explanation to the residents about why these
legal cases continue to be considered in closed session. He criticized the spending of thousands of
dollars on legal fees and pointed out that this should be provided to the public.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: She pointed out that half million dollars has already been paid out in attorney
fees to keep the council in office which thus resulted in the current lawsuit. She stated that the
legal briefs should be posted online so the residents can make their own determination. Criticized
the City Attorney for dismissing her comments on the legal process. Lastly, she addressed item 7
and criticized the spending of anymore money on this project.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley asked the City Attorney to clarify some of the accusations that were made
by public speakers and Mayor Goodell asked if the City Attorney could clarify the terms. Attorney
Curley provided a response.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 7 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

33. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced there will be a Sober Living Roundtable on Friday March
10. She stated there is legislation at the State level with a bi-partisan approach. She referenced an
Orange County Register reporter Teri Sforza on her investigative reporting on this subject.
Council Member Bucknum stated the bottom line is we want to protect the people being treated at
these sober homes. She mentioned the amount of snow in the Tahoe area and cautioned drivers.
Lastly, she reminded residents that the City offers filled sandbags for free during the rainy season
and the locations are City Hall, Community Center, Animal Shelter, and Alicia Park.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch announced that the Orange County Fire Authority will be hosting an
open house this Saturday, March 4 from 10:00 am to 3:00 pm and he encouraged residents stating
it is a very cool place. There will be many activities and food. He stated met with Fire Chief
Fennessy and toured all three of our fire stations. Council Member Ruesch said that he had the
opportunity to visit the Coastal Fire in Laguna Niguel to look at mitigated issues in the back side
of Mission Viejo which is similar to the Laguna Niguel area. He announced that in March there
will be a Vector Control presentation from the Director of Orange County Vector. Council
Member Ruesch also attended the Mass Shooting & Critical Incident Preparedness Forum. He
participated in the Oso Fit 5K in the rain and had a great time. Lastly, he stated he attended the
Investment Advisory Commission Meeting and was very impressed with the work that they do
and their knowledge.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated that she also attended the Mass Shooting & Critical Incident
Preparedness Forum and commented that it provided a lot of useful information. She went on a
ride along with the Orange County Fire Authority. Council Member Vasquez stated she also
attended the Oso Fit 5K which was cold but a lot of fun. She had the opportunity to meet with the
Director of Library Services to learn about the programs that are offered, and met with Melanie
McGrane at the Community Center to learn more about the senior programs provided.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that she also attended the Mass Shooting & Critical Incident
Preparedness Forum which was held on February 16 with several council members and staff. She
attended the Mission Viejo Police Services Academy and complimented Chief McDonald on his
City Council Minutes  9  February 28, 2023
 presentation and was impressed with the participation of our citizens. She commended the staff on
the Oso Fit 5K.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell stated that he also attended the Mass Shooting & Critical Incident Preparedness
Forum which provided a lot of good information that he would like to eventually incorporate some
of this information with similar training as the Police Services Training Academy. He said a few
years ago he attended the training academy and learned so much about what is going on in our
community. He congratulated those that have chosen to participate in this academy. He attended
a tour of the Morning Star Senior Living Facility and announced that the grand opening will be
Thursday, March 9 at 1:00 pm. He spoke about the marketing efforts for the 2028 Olympics. He
stated that he had the opportunity to meet with the director of the Oceania National Olympic
Committee Organization which represents various Pacific Countries and gave him a tour of our
facilities for training camps for the 2028 Olympics. Mayor Goodell said he has been invited to
attend their planning meeting with all those countries present in Brisbane, Australia in the middle
of April. He said he is working with the City Manager and staff to evaluate and put together a
plan. Lastly, he stated this will be an exciting opportunity for us to lay out the welcome mat in
Mission Viejo for our community to get exposed to the Olympic movement and it would also be
an economic generator for our businesses.
